adaptation.algorithm_identity: Theorem 6.3: BatchIterations.algorithm (SGD steps with the replies, uniform output) against the iteration-level oracle answering Malenia's estimator. Theorem 6.4: MaleniaUniform.malenia (Method 4 event by event: all workers start at x^k, every received gradient increments B_j and g_j and restarts worker j, the round ends when the harmonic mean of the counts reaches S/n, then x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma (1/n) sum_i g_i/B_i and all workers restart).
adaptation.cost: Theorem 6.3: one template call per iteration, budget max 1 ceil(24 L Delta/eps) + extra = K. Theorem 6.4: one template call per worker-completion event. The number of events Method 4 needs is not a function of the scalar parameters (it is at most sum_i floor(V_i(tbar_K)), which involves integrals of the powers, floors and the deadline, none of which the budget renderer can display, and it is undefined when tbar_K = infinity). The execution length is therefore an explicit natural parameter calls with budget p := p.calls (renders as calls, defined for all parameters), and successful assumes calls >= sum_i floor(V_i(tbar_K)) next to tbar_K < infinity; every run that finishes by tbar_K is covered by some calls and extra calls are idle. The source headline (time tbar_K) is the almost-sure bound on the returned clock.
adaptation.output: Theorem 6.3: a uniformly random iterate among x^0..x^{K-1} (its expectation is the source average). Theorem 6.4: (uniformly random iterate among x^0..x^K, elapsed clock); the average over K+1 iterates is bounded by Theorem 6.3 since K+1 >= 24 L Delta/eps.
adaptation.probability: Both setups take an abstract law P of a sample stream with StochasticGeneralized.IID coordinates of law mu (no prescribed product measure); round arrays are read from the stream by the fixed injective indexing arrays xi r c = xi (Nat.pair r c). Theorem 6.3: the oracle law is the image of P under arrays (call r reads array r). Theorem 6.4: every call sees the same arrays (image of P under xi |-> (fun _ => arrays xi)). The product representation (independent i.i.d. arrays) is derived inside the proofs from independence (arrays_law). Seeds of the template run: uniform index (algorithm law) x the oracle law.
adaptation.public_information: Theorem 6.3: Public = BatchIterations.Public (d, gamma, S, x0, N); f, the local functions, the oracles and the batch counts are hidden. Theorem 6.4: Public = (d, n, gamma, S, x0, K); the computation powers are not given to the algorithm: they only determine the event oracle (the times of the replies), matching Method 4 which waits for the next worker.
adaptation.source_correspondence: Theorem 6.3 = MaleniaIterations.result via malenia_accuracy (HetVar: estimator_moments; SGDtv: sgd_average); Theorem 6.4 = MaleniaUniform.result conditional on tbar_K < infinity; Exec64 (execute_malenia, round_step_h) transports the event execution of Method 4 to the SGD form with counts satisfying the exit condition and bounds the clock by tbar_K; lemma:min_inf (floor_min_attained) and the continuity of V_i (work_properties) are proved.

deferred_obligations.requirement: execute_malenia proves that the template run of malenia against eventOracle returns the Malenia SGD iterate x^j (counts satisfying the exit condition, environment samples) and a sample-independent clock c with ofReal c <= deadline whenever deadline < top and calls >= sum_i floor(V_i(deadline) - V_i 0).
malenia_accuracy derives eps for S = max{ceil(v/eps), n}, gamma = min{1/L, eps S/(2 L v)} (1/L if v = 0), every count schedule satisfying the exit condition and every K >= 24 L Delta/eps, K > 0.

result combines work_properties, the threshold inequality, execute_malenia, environment_transport, arrays_law, estimator_moments, sgd_moments, malenia_accuracy (K+1 iterates) and uniform_prefix_accuracy.

arrays xi r c := xi (Nat.pair r c) (round-r array read from a sample stream xi : N -> Omega); iterOracle p n B P g (P an abstract law of the sample stream): Seed r = (N -> Omega), law = image of P under arrays, answer r x seed := estimator (B r) g x seed (one call per iteration, round r uses counts B r); roundTime V eta s : ENNReal := if some t >= 0 has all floors floor(V_i t - V_i s) >= 1 and eta <= ((1/n) sum_i 1/floor_i)^{-1} then ofReal (sInf of that set) else top; deadline V eta : N -> ENNReal, 0 at 0, top propagates, else roundTime at the previous value (tbar_k of eq:upper_bound for general W, eta); Public (d, n, gamma, S, x0, K); Query := Option (point, start times, round, counts); Reply := Option (worker, time, gradient); eventAnswer (Option.elim form): on some (x, starts, r, B) returns the earliest finishing worker i (RennalaUniform.earliest of RennalaUniform.completion), its finish time and g_i(x, seed r (code n i (B i))); eventOracle p V P g: Seed k = (N -> N -> Omega) for every call, law = the image of the stream law P under xi |-> (fun _ => arrays xi) (every call sees the same environment arrays); State (round, counts, sums, point, starts, clock, chosen, selected); step: on (i, t, g) add 1 to counts i and g to sums i; if harmonicReady then x' = point - gamma (1/n) sum_j (1/B_j) sums_j, round+1, counts/sums reset, all workers restart at t, selected := x' if chosen = round+1; otherwise worker i restarts at t. malenia p: Seed Fin (K+1) uniform; initial j = round 0, zero counts/sums, all starts 0, chosen j, selected x0; query none once round >= K, else some (point, starts, round, counts); update identity once round >= K; output (selected, clock).
edge_cases: Workers that never finish are skipped; if nobody finishes, the state is unchanged.
Ties go to the lowest worker index; times and iterates do not depend on the tie rule.
The stopping rule is checked after each event; with zero counts it is false.
Samples of different (round, worker, count) are distinct positions of the round arrays (code is injective).
